analysis.title: GS Bartlett - GS TMT TODAY 10.8.26
key_insights: Futures are lower (Nasdaq -70bps, S&P -50bps, Russell -90bps). The two main macro inputs, oil (WTI +5%) and rates (US 10-year at 5.35%), are moving adversely.

An Atlantic report says the White House asked the Pentagon to draw up strike options against Iran that could be executed before the midterm elections. Crude rose on it, along with an approaching Gulf of Mexico hurricane and Houthi strikes on two Saudi airports that killed three people.
Fed Gov. Waller said further rate hikes will likely be needed. He said the Fed has flexibility on timing and does not need to tighten at consecutive meetings.

Samsung's 3Q26 preliminary operating profit of W107.4tn was in line with GSe and Bloomberg consensus (~W106tn). Investor expectations had slipped below W105tn, so GS says it was likely a slight beat versus the latest estimates. The stock fell about 3% in Korea and Kospi fell 260bps. Korea is lower in 6 of 8 sessions.

GS expects Samsung's memory profit to have been slightly better than expected on strong DRAM and NAND margins and robust HBM revenue. Memory supply tightness is lifting ASP expectations for both conventional memory and HBM.

GS believes Samsung's DRAM and NAND bit shipment growth was slightly below company guidance and GS estimates, due to limited supply and low inventory. The smartphone loss was likely smaller than feared on a richer mix toward high-end phones.

TSMC's quarterly revenue rose 51% to NT$1.49 trillion ($46.7bn, Bloomberg calculation) against an analyst average of NT$1.46 trillion. September monthly sales rose 55% y/y. The stock was down about 1.5% pre-market.

GS upgraded Palantir to Buy from Neutral with a $230 12-month price target (18% upside). The reasons are a possible step-change in addressable market from sovereign AI, bespoke applications and verticalization, and a forward-deployed-engineer model that Palantir can now automate with AI engineers. Palantir has an $8bn revenue run rate and about 100% growth. The stock is up 16% YTD versus NDX +24% and trades at a discount to growth comps on EV/FCF. The stock rose about 2.5% pre-market.

GS downgraded Tyler Technologies to Neutral from Buy and cut the 12-month target to $345 from $395, about 4% upside. The cloud thesis has largely played out and visibility into the next catalyst, including AI, is limited.

GS's Online Travel Q3'26 preview (Sheridan) describes end demand as broadly stable to strong, most pronounced in the US in the September quarter. The topics to watch are forward commentary on unit pricing, how management frames agentic AI, and the balance between growth investment and 2027 margins.

Dell'Oro expert call: AI infrastructure investment continues to be justified by capability gains rather than returns, and likely will for several years. Data center capacity should rise about 200GW over 5 years to about 250GW by 2030, with on-site generation increasingly important.
In networking, GS says ANET is among the best positioned in scale-across networks, CLS and HPE likely lead in scale-up, and CSCO has made impressive progress in scale-out.

European indices are lower (FTSE -60bps, DAX -1.1%, CAC -1.1%) with energy outperforming and financials and healthcare lagging. France's debt situation is in focus, with Bloomberg noting it is now riskier than 38% of the nation's company bonds.
Asia finished lower (Shanghai -79bps, Hang Seng -1.43%, Nikkei -1.42%, Kospi -2.62%), with tech lagging especially in mainland China after Golden Week and in Korea.
Today's US calendar: Initial Jobless Claims at 8:30am, Fed Pres. Musalem at 1:40pm, PEP reports pre-open.
